datasheet.title: UfiSpace S9311-64D 400GE Data Center Switch Datasheet

devices.description: UfiSpace S9311-64D 400G data center spine switch - 2RU white box, 64x QSFP-DD 400G in four rows of sixteen (two 2-high stacked cage banks) plus 2x SFP+ 1/10G, an RJ45 out-of-band port, RJ45 and micro-USB consoles, USB 3.0 and a 1PPS/10MHz SMB timing pair, on Broadcom Tomahawk 4 at 25.6 Tbps; four hot-swap fans (3+1) and dual 2400W PSUs (1+1) at the rear, orderable in AC or DC and in front-to-back or back-to-front airflow

gaps.note: The HIG's section 10 tables the six front-panel lamps, the PSU and Fan FRU lamps and the RJ45 management jack, and says nothing about the port lamps. Each QSFP-DD column carries a four-part cluster - a two-window light pipe at each end of the cage width with a round lamp inboard of each - and nothing states which half serves the upper port and which the lower, nor what the pipe's two windows mean against the round lamp. Every lamp keeps the component's off/on default; each cluster's `for` lists the two ports of the column it stands over, which is adjacency and not an asserted mapping. The SFP+ pair has no lamps drawn beside it at all.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: The HIG Component Physical Information table gives the fan module 81 x 176.53 x 81.5 mm (W x D x H). HIG Figure 9's rear elevation, which passes the aspect gate at 0.45%, draws four identical faces abutting from x 17 to x 837 px with no chassis web between them, and four independent repeated features on that face - the airflow tag, the status lamp, the handle and the release tab - all sit on a 205.33 px pitch, which is 83.84 mm. The face is 83.7 x 80.0 and the table's number is 81 x 81.5. The likely resolution is the S9300-32D's: 81 measures the fan BODY behind the flange and the face is wider. That is an inference and not something either document says, so the manifest carries the measured face and this entry carries the disagreement.
gaps.wanted: a vendor mechanical drawing of FAN-805616, or a caliper on the FRU

gaps.note: The ports ARE numbered 0-63 and 64-65 - HIG Figure 10 prints every numeral - but it prints them on the schematic module faces, where a seated module would cover them, so the figure does not say where the metal carries them. Nothing was found on the metal: the dark chassis web between the two cage bands profiles flat with no bright marks, and the 520 px front photograph is 1.19 px/mm, far too coarse for a 2 mm digit. No numerals are therefore drawn, rather than 66 of them being placed by guesswork.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on front photograph at 4 px/mm or better, or a vendor faceplate artwork sheet

gaps.note: Every small legend on the left-hand block is 4-6 px tall in the only orthographic front figure held, and does not resolve at 20x with autocontrast. Their positions and extents are measured; their WORDING is the HIG Figure 4 callout list and the Front Panel LED table's row names, which is a strong inference and still an inference. Four glyphs ARE legible and are drawn as seen: an up and a down triangle above the SFP+ block and another pair beside the RJ45 stack, plus the three-box network symbol to the right of the second pair. Three legends that certainly exist are NOT drawn, because nothing identifies them: a roughly 6 mm word between the USB symbol and the lower up-triangle at x 18.7-24.7 y 77-80, and two small marks flanking the SFP+ triangles at x 20.3-22.7 and x 32.9-35.4, y 12.7-15.3.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on front photograph at 4 px/mm or better

gaps.note: The HIG states the 110 V AC per-supply output twice and differently. Section 7 says 'If power input for AC power supply is only 110V, there will only be 1000 watts per power supply and will not be enough power for the power supply to be changed while the switch is in operation.' Section 9's AC note says 'If only a 110V AC power source is available, the S9311-64D can still be powered with both PSUs providing 1200 watts each for a total output of 2400 watts.' Same measure, same scope, two values. Neither is the number this manifest carries - power-output-w on the PSU contracts is the 2400 W nameplate from the datasheet's ordering lines, at the 200-240 V input the datasheet specifies - but a reader budgeting a 110 V feed needs to know the guide contradicts itself.
gaps.wanted: the PSU-242 supply datasheet, or a UfiSpace erratum for HIG R1.2

gaps.note: No held figure shows a DC build seated in the chassis. HIG Figure 9 and the datasheet rear render both show the AC unit with its C20 inlet, so the DC contract's fan frame, pull bar, latch and lamp positions are carried over from the AC unit rather than measured on a DC face. What is specific to the DC unit - a two-row input block, V+ over V-, with two lug/screw holes above it - comes from HIG Figure 6's CAD front view, whose own scale is only good to a couple of percent, so the block is drawn on the AC inlet's measured footprint instead of on that sheet's scale. gaps.note: The HIG says 'The 400G QSFP-DD ports highlighted support both ZR+ transceivers up to 32 units' above Figure 12, and Figure 12 renders the lower band of 32 ports (32-63) pale against the upper band's normal dark. 32 is exactly one band, so the count and the shading agree - but the guide never says whether the pale band is the highlighted set or the excluded one, and the sentence's 'highlighted' is not defined anywhere in the document. No port is therefore given a per-port ZR attribute; the capability is recorded on the device as 'up to 32' without naming which 32.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace optics compatibility matrix, or a Figure 12 revision with a legend

THAT WARNING IS LEFT STANDING because it is true and it is this gap's own record - the optics list is correct and nothing in the toolchain can currently reach it through the media name.

devices.description: UfiSpace S9600-32X open aggregation router - 2RU disaggregated white box on Broadcom Qumran2c with 2.4 Tbps of switching and 4 GB of deep buffer, carrying 32x QSFP28 40/100G in eight two-high stacked columns plus 4x SFP28 1/10/25G that break out from 100G port 0, and a full timing block (GNSS on SMA, 1PPS and 10MHz on SMB, ToD on RJ45, Stratum 3E OCXO, SyncE, 1588v2 Class C and TSN); four hot-swap fans (3+1) and dual 1600W supplies (1+1) at the rear

gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the six front-panel lamps (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID), the PSU FRU lamp and the Fan FRU lamp, and gives NO table for the port lamps. The sixty-four lane lamps drawn here therefore keep ufispace/lane-led-quad@1's off/on default rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. Nothing states whether the four lamps above a cage are four lanes, or a link/activity pair per breakout, or something else; the component's own provenance reaches the same conclusion from a different platform's guide.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: The four SFP28 ports have no lamp of their own. Eight lamp groups are drawn in each band and there are eight QSFP columns, so none is spare, and the guide never mentions an SFP28 indicator. What the faceplate does say is that the first QSFP column's two lamp rows are painted yellow and orange, continuous with the SFP28 legend band, where every other column's are green - and the guide says those four ports are the breakout of port 0. The natural reading is that port 0's four lane lamps are the four SFP28 ports' lamps in breakout mode. It is a reading and not a statement, so the lamps here are attached to port-0 and port-1 and the SFP28 group carries no indicator.
gaps.wanted: a NOS LED table naming the breakout lamps, or a photograph of a unit with the breakout enabled and one SFP28 port linked

gaps.note: Three UfiSpace chassis guides dimension the same fan SKU three ways. gaps.note: ufispace/psu-162-dc@1 records that no held figure showed a DC unit seated in a chassis, and built its face from the AC unit's with a terminal block on the inlet's footprint - grille left, connector right. gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the five front-panel lamps, the PSU FRU lamp and the fan FRU lamp in full, and says nothing at all about the port lamps. So the eight four-lamp strips beside the QSFP28 block are drawn because the figure draws them, at a pitch that matches ufispace/lane-led-quad's own to a hundredth, but what the four dots mean - four lanes, link and activity pairs, something else - is not stated, and neither is which of the two rows in each strip belongs to which port of the pair. gaps.note: THE 64 SFP28 LAMPS ARE THE TRIANGLES IN THE YELLOW BAND, and this gap used to say they did not exist. It said the hardware almost certainly had them, that HIG Figure 8's pale strip UNDER each module resolved to about two pixels at 9.585 px/mm, and that rather than invent 128 positions no reading supported, none were drawn. The search was in the wrong place: the lamps are above the modules, not below them, and the drawing already carried them - as 32 silkscreen marks reading `▲▼`, one per port pair, printed on the band. An up triangle for the top-row port and a down triangle for the bottom, which is the idiom the sibling S8901-54XC models correctly with common/led-arrow. Measured off the same figure, from the dark ink inside the yellow band rather than from a green cast beside it: each triangle is 2.35 x 1.47 mm, the two of a pair sit 2.79 mm apart, and the pairs repeat on a 14.37 mm pitch which is the port pitch. devices.description: UfiSpace S9610-36D 400G open core and aggregation router - 2RU white box, 36x QSFP-DD 40/100/200/400G in two rows of eighteen (one 2-wide and four 4-wide belly-to-belly cage banks) with OpenZR+/ZR on the whole upper row, plus a stacked 10G SFP+ management pair, an RJ45 out-of-band port over a USB 3.0 over an RJ45 console, a micro-USB console, 1PPS and 10MHz SMB timing jacks and a two-digit status display, on Broadcom Jericho2c+ at 14.4 Tbps with 16 GB of deep buffer, an OP2 external TCAM and a Stratum 3E OCXO; four hot-swap fans (3+1) and dual 3000 W PSUs (1+1) at the rear, orderable AC or DC

gaps.note: The HIG's section 10 tables the five front-panel lamps, the PSU and Fan FRU lamps and nothing else. It says nothing about the thirty-six port lamps, nothing about the two lamps in the out-of-band jack, and nothing about the two above the SFP+ pair. Which port each QSFP-DD lamp serves IS known - the arrow printed beside it says so - but what green, amber or blinking mean there is not, so every lamp keeps common/led-dot's plain off/on default rather than an invented vocabulary. The two SFP+ lamps sit above the UPPER cage with nothing below the lower one, so they cannot be one-per-port by position; they carry `for:` both ports, which is adjacency and not an asserted mapping.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: The numeral tiles for ports 1, 17, 19 and 35 are drawn yellow and the other thirty-two blue, because every image held shows them that way - HIG Figures 8b and 9b, which are marked-up, AND the vendor front and angle product renders, which are not captioned as marked up. Those four are exactly the set HIG Figure 8b calls 'Ports disabled when statistics counter is enabled'. The open question is whether the yellow is really on the metal or whether the product render is the same marked-up artwork with its caption removed, which is a thing this vendor does. The drawing is correct either way about WHICH ports they are; only the colour of four tiles is at stake.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of a real S9610-36D faceplate, or the vendor's artwork sheet

gaps.note: The two-digit seven-segment readout at x 4.70-17.51 is drawn in every figure and named in none. HIG Figure 4's callout list runs RJ45, Reset, Beacon LED, 1PPS, 10MHz, USB, System LED, Micro USB, RJ45, 2 x SFP and 36 x QSFP-DD; the nearest callout, 'Beacon LED', points into this block but is a lamp's name, and section 10's LED table has no row for a numeric display. Whether the digits show a POST code, a chassis or stack ID or a fault code is unstated, so the component carries no state vocabulary and its skin draws the all-segments '8.8.' the vendor's own artwork draws.
gaps.wanted: a NOS or BMC reference that documents the front-panel numeric display

gaps.note: Neither this datasheet nor this HIG gives the fan module a wattage. Searched both documents for 'watt', 'W)' and 'power consumption': every hit belongs either to the PSU-302 ordering lines (3000W), to the system maxima (1728 / 1752 / 2049 / 2073 W) or to the typical figure (767 W). The L27/L29 warning this device carries for the fans is therefore left standing, and the modelled module total is a floor rather than a total.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace FAN-808012 specification, or a measured figure from a live unit

gaps.note: This datasheet's Available to Order line reads 'FAN-808012-HC'; the S9321-64E datasheet the component was built from reads 'FAN-808012-HCE', and the two HIGs give the module different depths for the same face - 151.3 mm here against 154.8 there, with the same 81 x 81.5 face and near-identical weight (737 g against 741). The base configuration therefore overrides the component's model attribute to FAN-808012-HC, which is what this product's own ordering line says, and the disagreement is recorded here rather than resolved: it is not knowable from the documents whether -HC and -HCE are one part under two spellings or two builds of one family.

gaps.note: No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and the HIG name the product only as S9610-36D, and the Available to Order block names only the two PSUs and the one fan. gaps.note: The HIG counts the rail hardware exactly - 'The chassis has 5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins', plus 'two M4 screws (one on each chassis side)' - and Figure 11 draws all six numbered 1-5 and (a), front to rear, without a single dimension. The six positions on each side face are therefore spread evenly over the middle of the 762 mm depth and are ESTIMATED. The count and the order are the vendor's; the spacing is not.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing of the chassis side, or a straight-on side photograph

gaps.note: The datasheet lists ONE fan and TWO supplies for this platform and all three are 'exhaust air flow', and the HIG's Cooling paragraph says 'The S9610-36D airflow direction is front-to-back' with no alternative. Unlike the S6301 and S9510 families there is no intake-flow sibling named anywhere, so no back-to-front configuration is modelled and the red handles and latches are not a variant marker here. devices.description: UfiSpace S9611-36D 400G open core and aggregation router - 2RU white box, 36x QSFP-DD 40/100/200/400G in two rows of eighteen with OpenZR+/ZR on the top row, plus 2x SFP+ 1/10G, an RJ45 out-of-band port, RJ45 and micro-USB serial consoles, USB 3.0 and a 1PPS/10MHz SMB timing pair, on Broadcom Jericho2c+ BCM88850 with an OP2 BCM16K knowledge base at 14.4 Tbps and 16 GB of deep buffering; Stratum 3E OCXO, SyncE and 1588v2 Class C timing; four hot-swap fans (3+1) and dual 3000 W supplies (1+1) at the rear, orderable AC or DC, exhaust airflow only

gaps.note: Every held image of this faceplate letters it S9610-36D: the S9611-36D HIG's own port-overview figures 8 to 11, the S9611-36D datasheet's front and rear views, and all three vendor renders. The S9611-36D and S9610-36D are a near-twin pair and UfiSpace has illustrated the S9611-36D's documents with the sibling's artwork. The silkscreen here prints S9611-36D on the reasoning that a router does not letter itself as a different product, which is a judgement and not a reading. Nothing else on the face is affected - the dimensions, port table, LED table and callouts in the guide are all written for the S9611-36D.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of a real S9611-36D front panel, or vendor faceplate artwork

gaps.note: The HIG's section 10 tables the five front-panel lamps, the PSU and Fan FRU lamps, and stops. Nothing states what a port lamp means - link, activity, fault, or a lane aggregate - and no colour but the artwork's unlit green is shown. WHICH port each lamp belongs to is not in doubt (the printed triangle beside it points at its column), so every lamp carries a single `for:`; only the vocabulary is missing, and each lamp therefore keeps the component's plain off/on default. The two lamps above the SFP+ stack are the weaker case: they sit side by side above the upper cage rather than one per cage, and are assigned left-to-port-0 / right-to-port-1 from the '0 up-triangle / down-triangle 1' legend directly above them, which is a positional reading and not a stated mapping.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: Four features on the left-hand column are on the metal in every image and are named in no document. Two shallow round blind bosses, a small textured square window that reads like a mesh or a sensor, and a pair of short rounded slots under the beacon display. HIG Figure 4's callout list runs Reset, Beacon LED, 1PPS, 10MHz, USB, Micro USB, RJ45, System LED and 2 x SFP, and covers none of them. They are drawn as panel decor at their measured positions and given no part identity, because guessing one would put a name in the tree that no source supports.
gaps.wanted: a labelled front-panel figure, or a photograph of a real unit at close range

gaps.note: The HIG's Component Physical Information table gives the fan module 81 x 151.3 x 81.5 mm (W x D x H). The module seams in HIG Figure 4's rear elevation, which passes the aspect gate at 0.37%, sit on a 121.4 px pitch, i.e. 83.5 mm, and the vendor rear render puts the same seams on 291.3 px, i.e. 83.95 mm - so the drawn faces are about 2.7 mm further apart than the table's module is wide. The likely resolution is the S9321-64E's, where the same 808012 fan measures 81 in the table and 83.2 across the drawn flange: 81 is the body behind the flange and the face is wider. That is an inference and not something either document says, so the manifest seats the table's 81 mm module on the measured 83.7 mm pitch and draws the difference as chassis web, and this entry carries the disagreement.
gaps.wanted: a vendor mechanical drawing of FAN-808012, or a caliper on the FRU

gaps.note: This HIG dimensions the fan 81 x 151.3 x 81.5; the S9321-64E HIG, from which ufispace/fan-808012@1 was built, dimensions the same 808012 series 81 x 154.8 x 81.5 and weighs it 741 g against this guide's 737 g. Face size and height agree exactly and only the depth and weight differ, which is what a suffix change (-HC here, -HCE there) usually is. The component is reused unchanged because nothing on the modelled face depends on the 3.5 mm, and the configuration overrides the model string to FAN-808012-HC, which is the part this datasheet actually orders.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace fan ordering guide covering both suffixes

gaps.note: HIG section 8 says the router 'can be grounded from the router's case and/or the power supply units (PSUs)', and both rear images show what that means: an earth symbol and a round stud on the lower left of each supply's own face, below its two status lamps. Neither ufispace/psu-302-dc@1 nor ufispace/psu-302-ac@1 contracts that stud - they were built from the S9321-64E, whose figures do not show it - and those components are shared with another platform, so it is recorded here rather than added to them from this device's evidence alone.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on elevation or photograph of a PSU-302 face at a stated scale

gaps.note: No held figure shows an AC build seated in this chassis. HIG Figure 4's rear elevation and the vendor rear render both draw the DC supply, so the `ac` configuration swaps in a contract whose own face was measured on the S9321-64E and not here. The bay geometry is identical (68 x 40.6 in both guides' tables), so what is unverified is the face artwork, not the fit.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph or elevation of an AC-configured S9611-36D

gaps.note: No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and the HIG name the product only as S9611-36D, and the Available to Order block names only the two PSUs and the one fan. The S9510-28DC precedent applies: that model's -BN0B/-BR1B SKUs surfaced from the owner and from no held PDF, so orderable SKUs for the AC and DC builds almost certainly exist. The configurations therefore carry no part numbers rather than invented ones.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or a quote naming the chassis SKUs

gaps.note: The HIG counts the rail attachment pins ('5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins') and the locking screws ('two M4 screws, one on each chassis side') and draws them in Figure 15 without a single dimension; no held figure shows the underside at all. The five pins are therefore spread evenly along the 762 mm depth and the compliance sticker is placed by eye - every position on the left, right and bottom faces is estimated, and it is the estimates on those three faces that keep this device out of `verified`.

gaps.note: UfiSpace has published a hardware installation guide for every other UfiSpace platform modelled in this library and none for the S9620 family. That single absence is behind most of the other entries here: no Component Physical Information table to check the FRU faces against, no front-panel or FRU LED tables, no Port Overview table stating the ID ranges, no space-clearance or grounding section, no rail or pin counts, and no orthographic top, side or bottom elevations. The whole model rests on one datasheet and its two embedded renders.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-32E hardware installation guide, or any UfiSpace mechanical drawing of this chassis.

gaps.note: the six system lamps sit beside a printed white legend box whose six words are unreadable at every resolution held - 11-px-tall smears at 9.17 px/mm on the only image of them. The names carried on the placements (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID) are the S9321-64E HIG's names for the same six-lamp column on the same vendor's 2RU faceplate, in the order that lamp column runs, and the glyph outlines here are consistent with them. THEY ARE A DIFFERENT PRODUCT'S DOCUMENT, and the reason is filed as sources-disagree rather than needs-photo because the disagreement is between what this device's artwork says (nothing legible) and what a sibling's table says, which is not the same thing as nobody having looked.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of the left end of the front panel, or the S9620-32E hardware installation guide's front-panel LED table.

gaps.note: not one lamp on this device has a documented meaning. The datasheet tables no LED behaviour at all, and the HIG that would carry the front-panel, PSU FRU and fan FRU LED tables does not exist for this family. So the six system lamps, the 32 per-port lamps, the six SFP-cage lamps and the supply's own lamp all carry positions and no states. Every other UfiSpace device in this library transcribes those tables in full; copying one across from a different SKU would assert this platform's behaviour from another platform's document, and the lamp names above are already one borrowing more than is comfortable.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-32E hardware installation guide, or a NOS LED table.

gaps.note: three unlabelled round openings about 6 mm across - one at (6.89, 48.80) on the front left, two at (430.66, 21.89) and (430.65, 71.54) on the front right - and a 2.0 x 30.9 dark slot at x 431.98-433.94. devices.description: UfiSpace S9620-40DG - 2RU 40-port open aggregation router on Broadcom Qumran3a BCM88490 with a 16 GB external deep buffer; 24x 1/10/25/50G SFP56, 12x 40/100G QSFP28 and 4x 400G (or 2x 800G) QSFP-DD, full timing (GNSS/1PPS/10MHz/ToD/BITS) with a Stratum 3E OCXO, MACsec on every port, two front-loading 1000 W PSUs and five rear hot-swap fans. gaps.note: the hardware numbers every port - numerals on the SFP56 blocks' teal strips, a pair on the pale strip under each QSFP28 block, one on the blue bar above each QSFP-DD cage - and none of them is legible. The only front image is 649 px wide for a 440 mm panel, so a numeral is three or four pixels tall, and there is no hardware installation guide to carry a Port Overview table. rel-pos is therefore positional within each family and no numerals are printed on the drawing. The datasheet's '40-port' phrasing hints at a single 0-39 range; where it starts is not stated and is not assumed here.

The isometric render adds 'ToD', 'BITS', 'GNSS ANT', '10MHZ' and '1PPS'; the six names in the status-lamp legend strip, the mark under the OOB jack and the two labels on the console/USB block stay illegible. datasheet.title: UfiSpace S9620-54DC 400G Open Aggregation Router Datasheet (rev 20260811V01)

devices.description: UfiSpace S9620-54DC 400G open aggregation router - a 1RU 440 x 480 mm white box on Broadcom Qumran3u BCM88400 at 1.2 Tbps with 4 GB of deep buffer, carrying 54 ports on one face: forty 1/10/25G SFP28 and eight 1/10/25/50G SFP56 in twenty-four belly-to-belly ganged columns, then four 100G and two 400G QSFP-DD in three more. A timing block down the left edge takes a GNSS SMA, 1PPS and 10MHz SMB and a ToD RJ45 against a Stratum 3E OCXO with SyncE, 1588v2 and an internal GNSS receiver; the management RJ45, serial console and USB 3.0 the datasheet lists appear nowhere on this face. Five hot-swap fans (4+1) and dual 750 W supplies (1+1) at the rear, orderable AC or DC, front-to-back

gaps.note: UfiSpace has published no hardware installation guide for the S9620 family - the intake's own coverage sheet records the miss for all three S9620 models - so this device is modelled from a datasheet and two product renders and nothing else. Everything a guide normally supplies is therefore absent here: no faceplate figure with numbered callouts, so no callout audit was possible and any feature the render does not show is not merely unmodelled but unknown; no front-panel or FRU LED table, so no lamp on this device carries a state vocabulary; no component dimension table, so the fan and PSU faces are the library's from a sibling platform; no rear elevation; no rail or grounding section. This is the single largest limitation on the model and every other gap here descends from it.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-54DC Hardware Installation Guide, when UfiSpace publishes it

gaps.note: The largest front image UfiSpace serves is 520 x 150 px, which is 1.125 px/mm and 0.89 mm per pixel. Every size token on the product page was probed (/image/5e/, /image/5g/ and eighteen others) and nothing larger exists; the datasheet's own copy of the same picture is 158 px native. The render passes Gate 1 on aspect (9.900 against 10.000) so its PROPORTIONS are trustworthy and the standard pitches confirm them across 24 columns to 0.3 mm - but no printed legend on this faceplate is legible, no connector keyway is readable, and every coordinate quoted here to a tenth is really good to about half a millimetre.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of a real S9620-54DC faceplate at 2000 px or better

gaps.note: The datasheet lists a 100/1000M RJ-45 management port, an RJ45 serial console port and a USB 3.0 Type-A port. NONE OF THE THREE IS ON THE FRONT FACE - the front render shows exactly one RJ45, inside the timing block, and no USB opening anywhere, and the whole left block is only 24 mm wide. They are therefore on the rear, which UfiSpace publishes no image of. So three documented ports exist on this device and are modelled nowhere, and the mgmt group is not declared at all rather than being declared empty.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph or the hardware installation guide

gaps.note: No rear image of this model exists - the vendor publishes a front and a 45-degree front angle and nothing else, and there is no installation guide. The inventory is sourced (five hot-swap fans in a 4+1 set, two hot-swap 750 W supplies in a 1+1 set, all exhaust, front-to-back) but EVERY REAR COORDINATE IN THIS FILE IS INVENTED: the 52.0 mm fan pitch, the x 12.0 start, the supplies at the right, the vertical centring. They are laid out the way the library's other UfiSpace 1RU boxes are laid out, which is a plausible arrangement and not this chassis's. Nothing else is drawn on that face for the same reason.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph of an S9620-54DC, or the hardware installation guide

gaps.note: The tile at x 78.2-105.5 carries six lamps - four green across the top, one green and one blue below - and a printed legend beside each. At 1.125 px/mm those legends are two pixels tall and cannot be read, so NO legend is printed in this drawing and the lamps carry positional ids. The arrangement is the S7801-54XS's exactly (four lamps with a blue ID lamp beneath the fourth), whose HIG names them SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1 and ID, and the extra green lamp under the first is where a timing platform's SYNC lamp sits on the S9610-36D. That reading is recorded here so the next reader has it; it is not written into the artwork, and no lamp carries a state vocabulary because no LED table exists for this platform.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-54DC HIG's front-panel LED table, or a legible faceplate photograph

gaps.note: The faceplate prints port numerals on the yellow, teal and blue bands - two glyph clusters per column are visible - and this render cannot resolve a single digit. The numerals drawn are reconstructed as 0-53 left to right, even on the top row and odd on the bottom, which is what every UfiSpace box in this library does and what the per-column up/down lamp pair implies. Two things are genuinely open: whether UfiSpace numbers the 400G pair first on this SKU rather than last, and whether the run starts at 0 or 1. The olive band under the four 100G ports carries no printing at all, so those four are drawn unlabelled.
gaps.wanted: a legible faceplate photograph, or the HIG's port map

gaps.note: PORTS 48-51 ARE DRAWN WITHOUT NUMERALS ON PURPOSE, AND THEY ARE THE ONLY FOUR OF FIFTY-FOUR THAT ARE. The olive band under the two 100G QSFP-DD columns carries no printing: crop the three bands side by side at 26x and the teal band to its left is packed with dark glyph clusters, two per column, while the olive band holds a white up-triangle at each end, a white down-triangle at each end, eight round lamps along its lower edge and nothing else, and the steel-blue band to its right carries light glyphs at both ends. The blue band is the control that makes this a reading rather than a resolution artefact: it is the same darkness as the olive one and its printing survives, so a legend on the olive band would have survived too. Numerically the olive band's upper half (rows y 91-93 px) is uniform where the teal and blue bands vary. The vent strip above the shell was checked as well and carries only the lamp row and its two triangles. So this faceplate appears to identify its 100G pair by band colour and row triangle rather than by number. Printing 48-51 would put ink on the drawing that is not on the metal, which is the one thing silkscreen must never do - so they are left off, and this entry exists so that a reader comparing the render against the photograph can tell a deliberate absence from an unfinished model. If a legible photograph ever shows numerals there, they belong on the band in the light fill the blue band uses, which is what is legible on an olive ground.
gaps.wanted: a legible faceplate photograph, or the HIG's port map

gaps.note: The silver strip between the upper and lower cage rows on all three QSFP-DD shells is FINELY MARKED, not blank, and this render cannot separate the marks. Rows y 73-78 px read 190 / 84 / 152 / 130 / 96 / 186, so there are two darker rows at 21.1 and 23.8 mm inside a lighter band - that much is solid, and it is what the drawing reproduces, as decor. What it will not do is name a count. A local-minimum scan finds a 4.44 mm rhythm, but the two 100G columns - which are identical hardware - put that rhythm at offsets 1.7/6.2/10.6/15.1 mm in one column and 4.1/8.5/13.0/17.4 in the next, asymmetric in opposite directions and disagreeing by 2.4 mm. Two identical columns cannot really differ; that is the signature of sampling a pattern finer than the pixel grid, and the residual darkness between the minima says the true pitch is about half, near 2.2 mm, which 0.89 mm per pixel cannot resolve. So it is not decided whether these are indicators or the ganged cage's gasket comb. Against them being lamps: each 100G port already carries four round lamps that DO resolve, four above the shell and four on the olive band below it, so strip lamps would give one port twelve indicators; and the pattern continues across the 400G column, which has no lamp row above it at all. Nothing is drawn as an LED here on that reasoning, and no lane count is asserted in either direction.
gaps.wanted: a faceplate photograph at 2000 px or better, or the HIG's port-LED figure

gaps.note: Two identical 8.0 mm SMB jacks sit at (29.3, 5.3) and (44.4, 5.3) with a printed legend beside each that this render cannot read. They are assigned 10MHz and 1PPS in the order the datasheet's Timing Interfaces row lists them, which is a convention, not a reading - and the S9610-36D prints its pair the other way up in a vertical stack, so there is no house order to fall back on either. The GNSS SMA is identified independently, by being the larger connector and the only SMA the datasheet lists.
gaps.wanted: a legible faceplate photograph

gaps.note: The ToD RJ45's latch direction cannot be determined: the opening is eleven pixels across and the notch that would settle it is one. The jack is drawn in std/rj45-ganged's own orientation. On a single jack this is cosmetic; it is recorded because the library has been caught by mirrored stacked pairs before and the check was genuinely run here rather than skipped.
gaps.wanted: a legible faceplate photograph

gaps.note: Each of the twenty-four SFP columns carries two small dark 1.8 mm squares on the silver inter-row strip, at 2.7 and 12.0 mm from the column edge, flanking the up/down lamp pair - 48 of them, counted. They are drawn as decor because nothing identifies them: they could be a second lamp per port drawn unlit, a shell fastener or a gasket feature, and with no LED table and no faceplate figure there is no way to choose. Drawing them as lamps would assert a per-port indicator this device may not have.
gaps.wanted: the HIG's front-panel figure, or a legible faceplate photograph

gaps.note: No document held states what any port lamp means. The geometry is read: one up-triangle and one down-triangle per SFP column, four round lamps above and four below each 100G QSFP-DD column, and two lamps below the 400G column with none above it. The last of those is measured rather than assumed - the vent perforation runs unbroken above the 400G shell where it is visibly interrupted above the 100G shell - but whether the 400G pair really has one lamp each, or a lane row this render cannot separate, is open. Every lamp keeps its component's plain off/on default. The strip between the two QSFP-DD rows is finely marked rather than blank and is drawn as a banded decor field of the measured tone; its marks could not be separated and are deliberately not modelled as lamps. See the qsfp-inter-row-marks gap, which carries the measurement that decides it.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-54DC HIG's LED tables, or a NOS LED reference

gaps.note: This datasheet's Fan Types line reads 'FAN-405636-HD, exhaust air flow'. The library has ufispace/fan-405637, built from the S9110-32X's guide, at 50.7 x 40.0 mm. One digit apart in a number that encodes the rotor, so the two are probably one family and possibly not one face. There is no S9620-54DC guide to measure the real module against and no image of it, so the component is reused with its model attribute overridden to FAN-405636-HD and the substitution recorded here rather than hidden. If the faces differ, five bays on the rear are the wrong width.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace fan ordering guide, or the S9620-54DC HIG's component table

gaps.note: No wattage for the fan module appears anywhere. The datasheet's Fan Types line reads 'FAN-405636-HD, exhaust air flow' with no figure beside it, and there is no installation guide to carry a component table. Both datasheet pages were searched at 200 dpi for every occurrence of 'W', 'Watt' and 'power': the only hits are the two PSU ordering lines (750W), the AC/DC input ratings and the single system figure (125 W typical, no transceiver). The L29 warning this device carries is therefore left standing, and the modelled module total is a floor rather than a total.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace FAN-405636 specification, or a measured figure from a live unit

gaps.note: This datasheet orders PSU-751-AESR-1C and PSU-751-DESR-1C; the library's psu-751 components were drawn for the S9110-32X, which orders PSU-751-AESR and -DESR at the same 750 W and the same input ranges. The '-1C' suffix is undocumented in any held file. The faces are assumed identical and the model attribute is overridden per configuration.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace power-supply ordering guide

gaps.note: Both supplies are orderable and no held image shows either one seated, because there is no rear image. The base configuration seats the DC unit, which is an arbitrary choice recorded as arbitrary - on the S9610-36D the same choice was settled by reading a terminal block out of the rear elevation, and here there is nothing to read.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph of a shipped unit

gaps.note: The angle render shows the left side face carrying a column of countersunk ear-mount holes near the front and a run of rail features along its length, and the lid carrying three long transverse stiffening ribs and a scatter of fastener dimples. The counts are read off that render at 45 degrees; NOT ONE POSITION IS DIMENSIONED ANYWHERE, so every coordinate on the four non-port faces is estimated and evenly spread. The bottom face is not shown in any image at all and carries only a compliance sticker at an estimated position.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing, or straight-on side and underside photographs

gaps.note: Three features on the left block are drawn because two independent images put them there and are not named, because with no guide there is no callout list to name them with: a 4.4 mm round icon at (72.4, 5.7) carrying a diamond-shaped glyph, between the model legend and the lamp tile, and two 2.7 mm dark circles at (6.2, 37.4) and (16.9, 37.4) under the ToD jack. A third, the 2.7 mm circle at (6.2, 14.5), is placed as common/reset-button on the reading that a recessed pinhole above a management jack is a reset - which every other UfiSpace box in this library has - and that reading is a guess too.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-54DC HIG's front-panel callout list

gaps.note: No held document prints an orderable chassis part number; the datasheet's Available to Order block covers only the two supplies and the one fan. The configurations therefore carry no part numbers rather than invented ones, as on the S9610-36D.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or a quote naming the chassis SKUs

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 7 bays (rear 7); `physical-context` on port groups qsfpdd-100g, qsfpdd-400g, sfp28, sfp56 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
the Nautobot exporter is not importable - unlocks NetBox / Nautobot device-type export

datasheet.title: UfiSpace S9700-23D 400G Disaggregated Core and Edge Router Datasheet

devices.description: UfiSpace S9700-23D 400G open disaggregated core and edge router - 2RU white box on Broadcom Jericho2 BCM88690 with an external OP2 BCM16K TCAM, 4.8 Tbps and an 8 GB deep buffer, carrying 10x QSFP-DD 100/400G SERVICE ports (four of them 400ZR/OpenZR+ capable, all breakable to 4x100G) and 13x QSFP-DD 400G FABRIC ports that connect only to a UfiSpace S9705-48D or S9725-64E fabric switch, which is what makes it half of a distributed disaggregated chassis rather than a standalone box; a management cluster of 2x SFP+ 10G, an RJ45 and a micro-USB console, an out-of-band RJ45 and a USB 2.0 Type-A; four hot-swap fans (3+1) and dual 2000 W PSUs (1+1) at the rear, orderable AC or DC, exhaust airflow. Sold by DriveNets as the NCP-10CD packet-forwarder of its Network Cloud DDC.

gaps.note: Whether the two rows of each ganged QSFP-DD shell mirror belly-to-belly or share one orientation is NOT resolved by any image held. At 3.14 px/mm a cage lip is one or two pixels and the luminance profile is consistent with both. The only positive reading is the row of small retention tabs the datasheet render draws under the top row and under the bottom row in the same relative position, which points to a common orientation, and that is why both rows are drawn unrotated here. The sibling S9600-56DX draws its 2-high blocks MIRRORED on its own figure's stronger evidence (a graded bezel band above one row and below the other, plus a white EMI strip between them), so the two models differ deliberately and neither should be changed to match the other without new evidence.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on high-resolution photograph of the faceplate with the cages empty

gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the four front-panel lamps (SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1), the PSU FRU lamp and the Fan FRU lamp, and gives no table at all for the per-port lamps. Each port carries exactly one round lamp on the printed band beside its numeral - that much is certain, because the count is one per port across both blocks and port 12 has exactly one - but nothing states what any of them means. Every lamp keeps the component default of off/on rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with known ports up, down and passing traffic

gaps.note: HIG section 10's Management port LED table names a Left LED (1G link and activity, green) and a Right LED (10M/100M link and activity, amber), so the two lamps and their vocabulary ARE sourced for this device. Where they sit is not: at 20x the figure resolves ONE small dark window on the LEFT of each jack's aperture, at (43.1-44.4, 68.1-70.1) for the out-of-band jack, and no matching window on the right. The two lamps are therefore drawn symmetrically in the aperture as the table requires, and the right-hand position is placement by symmetry rather than by measurement. The upper (console) jack shows the same single left-hand window; the guide tables no lamps for a console port, so none are drawn there.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on high-resolution photograph of the stacked management jacks

gaps.note: A thin dark slot 42.0 x 1.2 mm sits near the bottom edge of the faceplate at (337.0, 85.4), under the fabric block and left of the model wordmark. It appears in HIG Figure 8, in the datasheet's product render and in the front photograph, carries no printed legend, and is named in no callout list. It is drawn as decor because it is unmistakably there; what it is - a vent slot, a label window, a light pipe - is not established. The S9600-56DX records the same unidentified slot in the same place on the same 436 mm faceplate.
gaps.wanted: a callout for it in a later revision of the guide, or a close photograph

gaps.note: FAN-803816-HC publishes no wattage. The datasheet names it only as an ordering line - 'Fan Types: FAN-803816-HC, exhaust air flow' - and the HIG carries no per-FRU wattage either; its Connecting Power sections give the SYSTEM maxima (993 W on DC, 987 W on AC) and the 2000 W per-circuit provisioning reserve, all three of which are the box and not the module. THE SEARCH WAS THE WHOLE INTAKE, not this document: the string FAN-803816-HC occurs in exactly three converted documents - the S9700-23D, S9700-53DX and S9705-48D datasheets - and in all three it is the same Available to Order line with no figure beside it, while a grep for 'watt' and 'power consumption' across this pair of documents returns only the system maxima, the 110 V derating note and the provisioning reserve. L27/L29 therefore stand against the four fan bays, and while they stand the chassis module total is a floor rather than a total.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace FRU datasheet for FAN-803816-HC

gaps.note: HIG section 8 says the grounding location 'is covered with a protective label' and step 5 says to remove it, but neither the rear elevation nor the rear product photograph shows a label there - both draw a bare silver two-hole pad. The pad is modelled as the two images show it. Whether the shipped unit has a label over it, and what colour, is not established here.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of an unopened unit's rear panel

gaps.note: No orderable chassis part number appears in any held document. The datasheet's Available to Order block lists the PSU and fan SKUs only, and the HIG names the product S9700-23D in its title, its overview and its dimensions table without printing a number. The configurations here therefore carry no `part-numbers`. This says only that we hold no document naming one, not that none exists.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or price list for the S9700 core-edge line

gaps.note: The HIG counts the side hardware - five rail attachment pins per side, ten in all, plus one M4 inner-rail locking screw per side positioned at the front - and dimensions none of it. The counts and the screw's end are the vendor's; every x position on both side faces is estimated at even spacing over the 762 mm depth. The faces are drawn rather than left size-only so the model reaches capability level 3, and this entry is the record that their geometry is a guess.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical side elevation, or a photograph of a chassis side with a rule in frame

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

a top-level `profile:` naming the device class, so that `specified` has something to judge the attrs against - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml for the classes that exist, which unlocks `specified` and with it the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 6 bays (rear 6); `physical-context` on port group qsfpdd-service - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
the Nautobot exporter is not importable - unlocks NetBox / Nautobot device-type export

datasheet.title: UfiSpace S9700-53DX 100G Disaggregated Core and Edge Router Datasheet

devices.description: UfiSpace S9700-53DX 100G open disaggregated core and edge router - 2RU white box on Broadcom Jericho2 with an OP2 external TCAM and an 8 GB deep buffer, 4.8 Tbps, built to run standalone or as a line node in a distributed disaggregated chassis behind an S9705-48D or S9725-64E fabric switch. Forty 40/100G QSFP28 service ports in ten four-high columns, of which ports 0-19 break out to 4x25GE or 4x10GE; thirteen 400G QSFP-DD fabric ports on a pink band at the right; two 10G SFP+ management ports, an RJ45 and a micro-USB console, a USB 2.0 Type-A service port, a 100/1000M out-of-band RJ45, a recessed reset and a two-digit beacon display. Four hot-swap fans (3+1) and dual 2000 W PSUs (1+1) at the rear, orderable AC or DC, front-to-back airflow

gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the four front-panel lamps (SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1), the PSU FRU lamp, the Fan FRU lamp and the management-port lamps, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. Every QSFP28 and QSFP-DD column prints two round lamps between its two port numerals and nothing states what they mean, nor which lamp of a pair serves which of the two ports. The pairing written here is derived from the printed order alone - the legend reads '▲n lamp lamp m▼', so the left lamp is taken to serve the upper port n - and port 12's single lamp is placed where a pair's left lamp sits for the same reason. That is the one thing in this device's LED model that is not read off a source. Every port lamp keeps the component default of off/on rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with known ports up, down and passing traffic

gaps.note: HIG Figure 4 names the two-digit seven-segment display 'Beacon LED' and the datasheet's LED list carries a 'Beacon' row, so unlike the S9600-72XC's identical-looking display this one at least has a name. What it DISPLAYS is still unstated: section 10's Verifying System Operation covers the four panel lamps and the two FRU lamps and never mentions it, so whether the digits show a chassis or cluster ID, a POST code or a fault code is not established. The component therefore carries no state vocabulary and its skin draws the all-segments '88' the vendor's own artwork draws.
gaps.wanted: a NOS or BMC reference that documents the front-panel beacon display

gaps.note: The bezel measured on this faceplate is 15.6 x 8.9 mm; ufispace/seg7-status-2@1 is 17.2 x 9.5, measured on the S9600-72XC, and is the closest of the three UfiSpace seven-segment contracts (the other two are 12.8 wide, a fifth too small). The part is used as it stands rather than forking a fourth contract off a 1.6 mm difference read from a 3.13 px/mm figure, but the placed display is about a millimetre larger than the metal.
gaps.wanted: an orthographic vendor front elevation of the S9700-53DX, or a square-on photograph

gaps.note: The reset feature on the panel is a white printed ring about 2.4 mm across around a dark pinhole about 1 mm across, measured at 20x on HIG Figure 8. common/reset-button@1 is 4.0 x 4.0 with `size: estimated` in its own provenance, so the library part is the softer number - but it is the part a person can name and it is used. The consequence is visible: the placed button laps roughly 0.9 mm onto the left edge of the printed system-lamp label block. Fixing it by moving the label block would move a measured number to suit an estimated one, so it is filed instead.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace mechanical drawing of the front panel, or a resized reset component

gaps.note: The datasheet orders PSU-202-DESR and the HIG has a full DC power section with its own maximum (1434 W), so the DC build certainly exists - but every image held for THIS device shows the AC supply: HIG Figure 7's rear elevation, HIG Figures 5 and 6 (which are the AC unit's own drawings), and the vendor's rear product render. The DC configuration here seats ufispace/psu-202-dc@1, whose face was measured on the S9600-56DX's rear photograph, and that is an inference from a sibling chassis rather than a reading of this one. The two routers order the same PSU part numbers, which is why it is reasonable; it is recorded because it is still not sourced here.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph or elevation of an S9700-53DX with DC supplies fitted

gaps.note: HIG Figure 7 carries no model name anywhere in it, and the S9700-23D's guide is illustrated with a rear elevation of the same fan and PSU arrangement. This family is exactly where a vendor reuses artwork, so the rear here cannot be certified as a picture of THIS model the way the front can - the front figures letter 'S9700-53DX' and draw this model's own port inventory. What supports the rear is not the figure: the FRU part numbers (FAN-803816-HC, PSU-202-AESR/DESR) and their dimensions come from this device's own datasheet and its own Component Physical Information table, the 4-fan and 2-PSU counts from Figure 4's callouts, and the vendor's rear product render of this SKU shows the same face. The geometry is the figure's; the inventory is this document's.
gaps.wanted: a rear elevation that letters the model, or a dimensioned rear mechanical drawing

gaps.note: The HIG counts the rail hardware exactly - five attachment pins per side, ten in total, plus one M4 inner-rail screw per side - and the vendor's angle render shows those pins as silver studs, so the COUNT and the KIND are sourced. No held figure dimensions them along the depth, and no held figure shows the underside at all, so every position on the two side faces and the compliance sticker on the bottom is ESTIMATED. They are drawn rather than left blank so the faces carry honest content, and this entry is what says which part of that content is a measurement.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace mechanical drawing of the chassis sides and underside

gaps.note: Neither held document names an optic for the two 10G SFP+ management ports. Searched the datasheet for 'SFP+' - three hits, all of them the port count in the physical list, the LED list and the Key Features - and its Compatible Transceiver Types and Compatible Fabric Cable Types blocks cover QSFP28 and QSFP-DD and stop; searched the HIG for 'transceiver' - its Connecting the Transceiver section is a procedure with no part numbers. So the group carries a sentence recording the silence rather than a list borrowed from a sibling datasheet.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace qualified-optics list for the S9700 series

gaps.note: No orderable chassis part number appears in any held document. The datasheet's Available to Order block lists the PSU and fan SKUs only, and the HIG names the product S9700-53DX in its title, its overview and its dimensions table without printing a number. The configurations here therefore carry no `part-numbers`. The S9510-28DC's history is the warning: 'no SKU exists' was written there on exactly this evidence and was false, so this says only that we hold no document naming one.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or price list for the S9700 core-edge line

gaps.note: Neither this datasheet nor this HIG publishes a per-FRU wattage for FAN-803816-HC. The datasheet names it only as an ordering line and the HIG's power sections give the SYSTEM maxima (1434 W DC, 1422 W AC, both at 45 C with optics fully populated and 100% traffic) and the 2000 W per-circuit provisioning reserve - all three are the box, not the module. Searched this HIG for 'watt', 'Power' and 'consumption': every hit belongs to the system figures or to the PSU-202 ordering lines. So the module total for this chassis is a floor, and L27/L29 standing on the fan is the record of that.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace FRU datasheet for FAN-803816-HC

datasheet.title: UfiSpace S9701-82DC High Density 25G Open Edge/Core Router Datasheet

devices.description: UfiSpace S9701-82DC high-density 25G open disaggregated core and edge router - a 2RU 436 x 609.6 mm white box on Broadcom Jericho2c BCM88802 with an OP2 BCM16K external TCAM, 2.4 Tb/s and 4 GB of deep buffer, carrying eighty-two ports on one face: sixty-four 1/10/25G SFP28 service ports in eight belly-to-belly ganged 2x4 shells, twelve 40/100G QSFP28 service ports in six stacked pairs, and six 400G QSFP-DD FABRIC ports - numbered 0-5 in their own space - that connect only to an S9705-48D or S9725-64E fabric to build a distributed disaggregated chassis. A timing block across the top left takes a GNSS SMA, a 10MHz SMB, a 1PPS SMB and a ToD RJ45 against a Stratum 3E OCXO with SyncE and 1588v2; below it sit two 10G SFP+ management ports, a 100/1000M RJ45, a USB 3.0 Type-A maintenance port and the RJ45 and micro-USB console pair, both lettered IOIOI. Four hot-swap fans (3+1) and dual 1300 W supplies (1+1) at the rear, orderable AC or DC, front-to-back

gaps.note: Each QSFP28 port's lane strip is drawn as ONE 14.4 x 2.6 opening, because the library cuts a lamp at its part's footprint and ufispace/lane-led-quad@1 is one part. The front render shows four discrete round lenses on the green band at a 3.94 mm pitch, each with its own dark ring, so the metal is four holes of about 2.4 mm and not a slot. Declaring the four would need four ids, and a cutout with no placement behind it is itself a finding, so the coarse opening stands until a drawing dimensions the holes. It is the same overstatement the arrow lamps carry, one order larger.
gaps.wanted: a panel-cutout drawing, or a photograph square-on to the green band at 2000 px or better

gaps.note: The white lozenge on each green band carries two dark glyph clusters - one on the up-triangle, one on the down-triangle - and neither source resolves them. Both images are the same raster at about 3.4 px/mm here, so a 1.5 mm numeral is five pixels. THE PRINTING IS THERE: the control is the crimson fabric band 25 mm to the right and the yellow SFP28 bands to the left, the same glyph size on grounds of the same darkness in the same crop, and both resolve cleanly. So this is an unresolved reading, not a blank area. The numerals drawn - 64/65, 66/67, 68/69, 70/71, 72/73, 74/75 - are the HIG port table's own range assigned in the order Figure 8 itself calls the shells out, so the VALUES are sourced even though the glyphs were not read. What is genuinely open is only their exact size and placement inside the lozenge.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on faceplate photograph at 2000 px or better

gaps.note: The green band under the lower QSFP28 row ends at x 337.2, so ports 74 and 75 have their eight lane lamps and their number lozenge printed on bare panel while the other five pairs have them on green. The band above the upper row runs the full width across all three shells. Measured independently in both images and they agree - guide figure 291.26-337.23, product render 291.19-336.75 - which is why it is drawn rather than tidied to match the top band. Recorded as sources-disagree because the two sources agree with each other and disagree with the device's own symmetry everywhere else on this faceplate; a photograph of a real unit would settle whether the metal is really printed this way or whether both renders inherit one artwork slip.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of a real S9701-82DC faceplate

gaps.note: HIG Figure 8 draws FIVE system lamps with a five-line plaque and the guide's own Front Panel LED table documents five - SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, each with its own state list. The vendor's front product render draws FOUR, on a plaque 9.4 mm tall instead of 11.7, lettered SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1. Five are drawn: the guide's figure and the guide's table are two statements in the device's own manual and they agree with each other, while the render is a product-page image that also disagrees with the guide about the QSFP28 lane lamp spacing. The render is probably of an earlier build or an earlier artwork.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of a shipped unit, or a guide revision that reconciles the two

gaps.note: No document held says what any PORT lamp means. Section 10 of the guide tables the five system lamps, the PSU FRU lamp, the fan FRU lamp and the management RJ45's left/right pair, and stops. So the geometry here is read - one up and one down arrow per SFP28 column, four lamps per QSFP28 port in two rows of four, one lamp per QSFP-DD fabric port - and every one of them keeps its component's plain off/on default rather than an invented vocabulary. The five system lamps and the two FRU lamps do carry the guide's real states.
gaps.wanted: the S9701-82DC's NOS LED reference, or a guide revision with a port-LED table

gaps.note: The two-digit blue seven-segment display at the top right of the faceplate appears in Figure 8 and in both product renders and is named in NO callout list, NO LED table and NO section of either document. It is drawn because three images put it there; what it counts, displays or beacons is not stated, so it carries no state vocabulary. Every other UfiSpace box in this library with the same display is in the same position.
gaps.wanted: a guide revision or NOS reference that documents the display

gaps.note: The legend row above the mgmt RJ45 / USB 3.0 / console RJ45 stack reads [LAN symbol] (up-triangle) (down-triangle) [SuperSpeed USB symbol]. The two symbols clearly name the RJ45 and the USB port; what the triangle pair names is not stated anywhere. On every other band of this faceplate that glyph pair marks the upper and lower port of a stack, so it is drawn attached to the two RJ45s on that reading - which is a reading, not a transcription, and it is recorded here rather than asserted in provenance as fact.
gaps.wanted: the S9701-82DC HIG's front-panel callout list

gaps.note: This datasheet orders PSU-132-DESR and PSU-132-AESR, both 'exhaust air flow'. The library's ufispace/psu-132-dc and -ac are PSU-132-DISB1 and PSU-132-AISB1, the INTAKE variants of the same 1300 W part at the same 50.5 x 40.0 face this guide's own component table states. The rear render's DC supply matches the component's drawn face feature for feature, and airflow is an internal-fan direction rather than a faceplate fact, so the components are reused with the model attribute overridden per configuration. What is NOT checked is whether the exhaust variants differ in any visible detail, because no held image shows a PSU-132-?ESR outside this chassis.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace power-supply ordering guide, or a photograph of a PSU-132-DESR

gaps.note: This guide's Component Physical Information table gives the fan as 3.19 x 4.45 x 3.21 in (81 x 113 x 81.5 mm); the S9600-28DX guide the library component was built from gives 80 x 113 x 81.5 for the same FAN-803816-HI part number. One millimetre of face width, two guides of the same vendor, same part. The component's 80.0 is kept so the library does not fork one part into two sizes, and the bays are laid on the measured 85.1 mm pitch, which is what actually positions them. Either figure sits inside that pitch, so nothing downstream turns on the choice.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace fan specification sheet

gaps.note: The guide states the count - 'The chassis has 5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins' - and that the inner rail is then locked with 'two M4 screws (one on each chassis side)' positioned at the front. NOT ONE OF THOSE POSITIONS IS DIMENSIONED, and the rack-mounting figures show the rail rather than the chassis wall, so all six features on each side face are estimated and evenly spread over the depth. The underside is not shown in any image held at all; the bottom face carries only a compliance label at an estimated position, and nothing else is invented for it.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing, or straight-on side and underside photographs

gaps.note: The five lid ribs are measured in plan from HIG Figure 4 - 400.3 mm wide from x 18.0, at y 118.6, 213.9, 309.9, 405.8 and 501.1 from the REAR, on a 95.6 mm pitch - and nothing states whether they are pressed grooves or raised stiffeners, or how deep. They are drawn as flat decor at the measured outline for that reason; no relief is claimed in either direction.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing of the lid

gaps.note: No held document prints an orderable chassis part number; the datasheet's Available to Order block covers only the two supplies and the one fan. The configurations therefore carry no part numbers rather than invented ones.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or a quote naming the chassis SKUs

datasheet.title: UfiSpace S9705-48D 400G Disaggregated Fabric Switch Datasheet

devices.description: UfiSpace S9705-48D disaggregated fabric switch - the 2RU 436 x 762 mm fabric plane of a Distributed Disaggregated Chassis, on a Broadcom Ramon BCM88790 switching cells rather than Ethernet frames at 8 billion cells per second, and scaling an S9700-series cluster to 691 Tb/s. The front face carries forty-eight 400G QSFP-DD fabric ports in twelve four-port blocks, each port with its own red numbered lamp tab, and a management cluster down the left edge: two 10G SFP+ management ports, an RJ45 serial console and a micro USB console both legended IOIO, a USB 2.0 Type-A, a 100/1000M RJ45 OOB port, a reset pinhole and the SYS/FAN/PS0/PS1 lamp column, with a two-digit beacon readout at the right. Four hot-swap fans (3+1) and dual 2000 W supplies (1+1) at the rear, orderable AC or DC, front-to-back. The fabric ports are cell based and interconnect only with the fabric ports of the S9700 series

gaps.note: Every one of the forty-eight fabric ports carries one lamp, on its own red tab, and NO HELD DOCUMENT SAYS WHAT IT MEANS. The HIG's section 10 has four LED tables - Front Panel (SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1), PSU FRU, Fan FRU and Management port - and none of them is about a fabric port; the datasheet's LED row lists 'Per port link status' and stops there. So each lamp keeps common/led-dot's plain off/on default rather than borrowing a link/activity vocabulary from a sibling guide. The lens is drawn dark because that is how the figure and the photograph both show it, unlit.
gaps.wanted: a NOS LED reference for the S9705-48D, or a later HIG revision with a fabric-port LED table

gaps.note: The two-digit seven-segment window at the top right is called 'Beacon LED' in HIG Figure 8's callouts and 'Beacon' in the datasheet's LED list, and nothing anywhere says what the digits show - a rack position, a stack id, a POST code, or simply a flashing locator. The component is placed as a display with no state semantics attached rather than having a meaning invented for it.
gaps.wanted: the S9705-48D NOS documentation, or an HIG revision that tables the display

gaps.note: Two guides give this supply two sizes. THIS device's HIG Component Physical Information table says 'PSU (W x D x H) 1.99 x 14.17 x 1.58 in (50.5 x 360 x 40 mm)'; the S9600-56DX HIG, which ufispace/psu-202-ac@1 and -dc@1 were built from, says 50.5 x 321 x 40.2 for the same PSU-202-AESR/DESR part numbers - while ITS OWN Figure 5 mechanical drawing dimensions the body at 360.0 mm, which is what this guide says. So the depth is 360 in two independent places and 321 in one table, and the face height is 40.0 here against 40.2 there. devices.description: UfiSpace S9710-76D - 2RU high-density 400G disaggregated core and edge router with 36 QSFP-DD service ports and 40 QSFP-DD fabric ports, 2x 10G SFP+ management uplinks and a full timing block; Broadcom Jericho2c+ BCM88850 at 14.4 Tbps with 16 GB of deep buffer, Intel Skylake-D 8-core with an AST2400 BMC, 1+1 hot-swap 3000W AC or DC PSUs, 3+1 hot-swap fans, front-to-back airflow. It runs standalone with loopbacks in the fabric ports, or as a line node in a Distributed Disaggregated Chassis cluster behind an S9705-48D or S9725-64E fabric.

gaps.note: whether the faceplate metal prints a numeral beside each cage is not resolvable from anything held. No numerals are printed here rather than printing ink the device may not carry.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of one cage block at 10 px/mm or better.

gaps.note: all 76 QSFP-DD ports and both SFP+ ports carry lamps, and the HIG's section 10 defines only the five system lamps (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1), the PSU and Fan FRU lamps and the management jack's pair. It gives no colour vocabulary for the port lamps at all, so the 38 clusters and the two SFP+ lamps here carry positions and no states. Nor does anything say what the pair of small round green lamps between each cluster's two windows is for; they are drawn because they are there. And three service clusters in the lower strip (ports 1/3, 21/23, 33/35) show an amber upper cell over a blue lower cell in the vendor render where every other cluster shows blue over blue - a lit state on the ordinary blue lens rather than a different lens, and one that matches no set the guide names, the OP2 ports included. What amber in the upper cell means is exactly the vocabulary the vendor does not publish.
gaps.wanted: a NOS LED table, or photographs of a live unit with known ports up and down.

gaps.note: a small dark rectangle 2.5 x 3.1 mm sits at (7.74, 28.26), between the seven-segment display and the 1PPS legend. gaps.note: the two-digit display under the model name is drawn in every figure and named in none: HIG Figure 4's callout list skips it and section 10's Verifying System Operation tables the five front-panel lamps and the FRU lamps without mentioning it. devices.description: UfiSpace S9720-56ED - 2RU 800G disaggregated core and edge router with 56 QSFP-DD cages in two bands: 36 service ports numbered 00-35, configurable in pairs as 18 x 800G or 36 x 100/200/400G with ZR/ZR+ support, and 20 x 800G fabric ports numbered 00-19 that make the box a line-card element of a distributed disaggregated chassis scaling to 921.6 Tbps. The 56 QSFP-DD lamps and the four above the SFP shell are drawn in every figure and named in none, so they carry positions and no states. They are drawn attached to the RJ45 OOB jack and the USB port on the reading that they are this vendor's stacked-pair up/down convention, the same one the SFP shell's own legends use two centimetres away; that reading is a judgement and is recorded here rather than left to look like something the guide says.

datasheet.title: UfiSpace S9725-64E 800G Disaggregated Fabric Router Datasheet

devices.description: UfiSpace S9725-64E - 2RU 64-port 800G QSFP-DD disaggregated FABRIC router on the Broadcom Ramon 3 BCM88920 cell switch, the backplane fabric element of a Distributed Disaggregated Chassis. Its 64 ports carry switching cells between S9700-series line-card boxes rather than customer traffic, and the vendor prints their numerals in magenta to say so. Two 10G SFP+ management uplinks, an Intel Ice Lake 4-core with an AST2620 BMC, 1+1 hot-swap 3000W AC or DC PSUs, 3+1 hot-swap fans, front-to-back airflow. Sold by DriveNets as the NCF-64E fabric element of the DDC Network Cloud.

gaps.note: HIG Figure 8 draws the 64 QSFP-DD cages in eight two-column ganged shells per band (bright seam runs 59.79-102.99, 106.54-149.29 ... at a 45.95 step, with no brightness dip at the internal column boundary). The vendor front photograph and the datasheet's own front view both draw SIXTEEN one-column shells per band on a uniform 22.7-22.98 step with an identical dark gap between all of them. All three agree on the port pitch, so nothing about port position turns on this; what turns on it is whether the metal between columns 2j+1 and 2j+2 is bright or dark. One shell per column is drawn, because two of the three sources show the shipped product and only one is a guide render.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of a populated port block, or a mechanical drawing of the cage assembly.

gaps.note: HIG Figure 8's body is 2.0% out in aspect, and the x scale is confirmed to 0.1% from outside the document by the sibling S9321-64E's independently measured column pitch. Nothing confirms the y. Every vertical number on the front face - band tops, row centres, lamp and legend baselines, the left cluster - is anchored only to the datasheet's 87.7 mm over this figure's 752 px and could be systematically 2% out; the horizontal ones are not affected.
gaps.wanted: an orthographic front elevation, or a vendor 3D model of the chassis.

gaps.note: the bottom face is sized from the chassis and carries nothing, because no image of the base exists anywhere in the intake. HIG Figure 4 draws top, front and rear; Figures 9-12 show the chassis from above and from the front-left on rails; Figures 19-21 show the rear grounding pad. The HIG text never mentions the underside either - searched for underside, bottom, base, rubber, feet, serial number, product label and nameplate across the HIG and the datasheet, and the only hits are the DC terminal block's cover, an ESD footwear caution and a GR-1089 cable-length warning. So the compliance/serial label field this class of box normally carries on its base is not drawn: its existence is a reasonable guess and its position and size would be pure invention, and there are no rack-ear or foot fixings to infer from - the chassis hangs on ten side standoff pins. This entry, not L45's warning, is the record.
gaps.wanted: a bench photograph of the underside, or a UfiSpace mechanical drawing showing the base.

gaps.note: the left and right faces carry five rail standoff pins each, which is the HIG's own count ('The chassis has 5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins') read off Figure 10's isometric, where they are numbered 1-5 with the M4 screw hole marked behind pin 5. The COUNT and the ORDER are the vendor's; the SPACING IS ESTIMATED - the pins are laid out evenly over the middle of the 762 mm depth with the screw behind the last, because no orthographic side elevation exists in the intake and an isometric gives no usable pitch. The sibling S9321-64E's file estimates the same spacing from the same sentences about the same rail kit, which is one estimate appearing twice and not corroboration.
gaps.wanted: an orthographic side elevation, or a rail-kit drawing dimensioning the pin pitch.

gaps.note: three round openings on the front carry no printed legend and no callout - 6.4 mm at (6.93, 33.18), the same size as the two SMB timing bezels but drawn black where they are yellow; 3.4 mm at (12.19, 8.66); and 3.0 mm at (19.0, 31.8). HIG Figure 4 names nine things in that area and none of them is any of these, and the datasheet lists exactly two timing interfaces. All three are drawn as dark decor circles so the panel is not silently missing its holes; guessing any of them into a connector would be inventing one.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the front panel's left end at a resolution that shows what is behind each opening.

gaps.note: an up arrow and a down arrow are printed between the network symbol and the USB SuperSpeed logo above the silver plate. HIG Figure 4's callouts name the three connectors under the plate and name nothing printed above it, and the three glyphs are side by side while the three connectors are stacked, so no positional rule assigns them. The pair is attached to the console jack here, which is what the sibling S9321-64E's file does with the same row on the same plate; it is a borrowed guess and not a reading of this device's own sources.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the plate at a resolution that resolves what each glyph sits over, or a vendor legend table.

gaps.note: every one of the 64 QSFP-DD fabric ports and both SFP+ uplinks carries a lamp on the strip beside it, and the HIG's Verifying System Operation section defines only the five system lamps (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1), the PSU FRU lamps, the fan FRU lamp and the management port pair. It gives no colour vocabulary at all for the port lamps, so the 66 placements here carry positions and no states.
gaps.wanted: a NOS LED table, or photographs of a live unit with known fabric links up and down.

gaps.note: the five system lamps sit beside a printed white legend box, but the best resolution the intake reaches on that block is HIG Figure 8 at 8.7 px/mm over an embedded raster of far less, where the glyphs are a grey smear. The names carried here (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1) are the HIG Front Panel LED table's own, in the table's order, which the lamp order matches and which the table's own opening sentence lists in the same order.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of the left end of the front panel.

gaps.note: HIG Figure 4 calls the two-digit seven-segment display 'Beacon LED' and that is the only thing any held document says about it. Section 10's Front Panel LED table covers SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0 and PS1 and stops, so what the digits show - a beacon or chassis id, a POST code, a fault code - is not stated and no state vocabulary is claimed. The artwork draws '8.8.', which is the all-segments lamp test rather than a value.
gaps.wanted: a NOS or BMC document describing the front-panel numeric readout.

gaps.note: HIG Figure 4's rear elevation and the vendor rear photograph both show the AC build, and HIG Figure 5 dimensions the AC unit. ufispace/psu-302-dc's face layout was estimated when it was built for the sibling S9321-64E and nothing in THIS device's intake improves it; the terminal block's size and position on the face remain the weakest numbers behind the dc configuration. The AC unit's face is measured, the DC one's is not, and the two must not be read as equally sourced.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on drawing or photograph of the PSU-302-DESR face.

gaps.note: 'FAN 0 1 2 3' is printed once on the chassis strip between the fan bank and the PSUs, which is modelled - but it is a single legend naming four bays rather than a per-bay mark, so nothing on the drawing ties bay 2 to the digit 2. Whether the hardware also prints a digit on or beside each bay is not resolvable from the elevation, where the fan modules cover whatever is behind them.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the rear with one or more fan modules removed.

gaps.note: ufispace/fan-808012 states no draw. This HIG dimensions the fan FRU, weighs it at 741 g and tables its LED without a wattage, and the datasheet names FAN-808012-HCE only as an ordering line; the only watt figures in either document are the two PSU ordering lines and the two system maxima. L29's standing warning is the live count of how much of the chassis total is a floor rather than a total.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the fan module's label, or a UfiSpace FRU datasheet.
